summary: A. P. Buddhadatta was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College and was a member of the Kalyanavamsa Nikaya (attested 1923).
A. S. Gadre worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of Archaeology for the Archaeology Department of Baroda State (attested 1944).

A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941) and as Superintendent in the Department of Archaeology, Travancore State (1922).

A. V. Williams Jackson worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University and studied at Halle-Wittenberg. He was an Adjunct Professor of English Literature (1883–1890) and Professor (1895–1935) at Columbia.
A.-Ferdinand Hérold was an Indologist. He was educated at the École Nationale des Chartes and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he earned a Licensié-ès-lettres.
Aalekhya Malladi specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at Emory University in 2022 and was appointed Assistant Professor at McGill University in 2023.

Aaron P. Proffitt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (c. 2009–2015) under Micah L. Auerback, and became assistant professor of Japanese Studies at the University at Albany, SUNY, around 2016.
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist who succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Abanindranath Tagore worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Government College of Art and Craft, and held a post at the University of Calcutta (c. 1921–1929).

Abdur Rehman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a PhD from the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1868) and the Sorbonne, becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE Linguistics in 1885.

Abel Hovelacque worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Honoré-Joseph Chavée and held posts at the École d'Anthropologie, where he was Professor of Linguistics (1876) and later Director (1891).

Abhijit Mandal specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He earned an MA at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira and a Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta (2014–2018). In 2016, he became an Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University.
Abhimanyu Rao is an Indologist who studied under Deepak Dabral. He holds a post at the Shiv Nadar School.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Abidin İtil was an Indologist who studied under Walter Ruben and earned his PhD at Ankara University (c. 1940–1944). At Ankara University, he taught Sanskrit beginning in 1936, served as Assistant (1943–1946), and was Professor and Department Head (c. 1964–1975).
Abigail I. MacBain works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008) and held a post at the University of Edinburgh in 2022.

Abigail Leach studied classics and Indology at Radcliffe, Vassar (A.B., A.M.), and Leipzig. She taught at Boston Latin Academy (1880–1883), chaired the Greek Department at Vassar College (1889), and served as President of the Society for Classical Studies (1898–1900).

Abirlal Gangopadhyay is an Indology scholar. He studied at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya, Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute, Jadavpur University, and completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hyderabad in 2023.

Abraham Anthony Fokker was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. from Leiden University (c. 1891–1894). He served as a professor at the University of Indonesia and taught Malay at the University of Amsterdam (c. 1919–1927).
